title: Rebuild CI to produce hermetic multi-arch artifacts with SBOMs and signed attestation
creator: Lena Park
description:
Goal: Replace ad-hoc Docker build steps across services with a hermetic, reproducible CI pipeline that produces multi-architecture (amd64 + arm64) images, generates SBOMs for each artifact, and signs attestation metadata. This reduces deploy drift, speeds engineer feedback via cache reuse, and enables downstream compliance checks for Private deployments.

Key outcomes we want:
- Deterministic artifact hashes for identical inputs across runner types.
- Cross-platform images built in CI with a single canonical build definition (buildx + buildkit + remote cache).
- Attached SBOM (CycloneDX) and cosign signature for all published images.
- Converged, hermetic toolchain images so lint/test steps do not mutate host state.
- Developer ergonomics: local dev can reproduce CI builds with the same toolchain image.

Scope: infrastructure + infra-ops + service build definitions. We'll touch the monorepo build matrix, the deploy manifests that expect image tags, and the internal artifact-retention configuration for the registry.

Non-goals: full image shrink/optimizations (separate perf ticket), audit of every third-party package in SBOM (we'll provide the SBOMs; triage in a follow-up).
comments: 2026-02-20 — Kickoff: Spike approved. Scope trimmed to core service images and base toolchain images (node/python/golang). Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Hermetic+Multi-Arch+Builds (draft).

2026-02-28 — Spike complete: PoC built using buildx + QEMU in ephemeral runners. PoC notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-pocs/pull/12. Observed cache miss pattern due to non-deterministic /tmp artifacts from test runners. Next: pin toolchain image + isolate test caches.

2026-03-03 — Decision: adopt a two-layer cache strategy: 1) content-addressable remote cache (registry-backed) for final image layers; 2) local buildkit cache priming for fast incremental builds. Trade-off: increased registry storage and retention policy complexity vs much higher cache hit rates across runners.

2026-03-05 — Linter/toolchain convergence: we'll stop installing global node_modules in CI and move linters into a hermetic toolchain image (node 20 + pinned eslint plugins). This removes per-run network installs that caused flakiness in previous pipelines.

2026-03-08 — Security review prep: SBOM generation step using syft (CycloneDX) is wired into the build pipeline. Need security SME sign-off prior to enabling attestation upload for production images. Ticket created for security docs (SEC-1207).

2026-03-10 — Benchmark: end-to-end cold build for service A (amd64+arm64) dropped from 24m to 16m using remote cache priming (cached base layers). Cache-hit incremental builds average 65s on a warmed runner. Raw logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/ENG-273981/runs/45.
2026-03-12 — Blocker: registry retention policy blocks inline cache export for arm manifests; Eng infra needs to extend TTL for cache tags (DEP-REG-42). Raised dependency with infra on 2026-03-12.

Next steps: (1) implement cosign attestation signing in pipeline (2) add SBOM upload to artifact storage and link from release notes (3) migrate remaining services in 2 waves: critical infra services -> product services.
